cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Prove We’re Close
cards.instruction: Get someone to take a social or emotional risk that demonstrates trust in the connection.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Come to the reunion with me. Let them see us arrive holding hands.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They still think we're just friends.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I know. I want us to trust each other in that room too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Last time someone asked, you let go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll introduce you as my partner. Will you keep hold while I say it?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 commands arrival but A3 and A5 request reciprocal trust without an operative superior permission tactic beyond the prefixed rank claims.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 friends assumption prompts A3 public trust aim; B4 prior letting go causes A5 explicit partner introduction and shared hold.

relationship.evidence: B2 states social risk and B4 identifies A past withdrawal, giving B a grounded reason to hesitate.

heightening.evidence: B4 prior failure causes A5 to take the naming risk first while asking B continued contact.

specificity.evidence: A1 reunion and B2 perceived friendship establish the public exposure; no external judgment specifics are needed.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 introduction while holding is earned, but the stock A3 command interrupts the sincere reassurance.
